## Statistical Validation: 11-4 Performance Analysis

August 28th provided an excellent sample size for model validation, delivering an 11-4 record (73.3% accuracy) that exceeds our baseline expectations. When we examine the probabilistic framework behind these selections, we see a pattern consistent with sound sabermetric principles: high-confidence picks performed reliably, while our two misses came in games with inherently higher variance.

## Confidence Calibration and Expected Outcomes

Our model's probabilistic outputs showed strong calibration today. The eight picks with 59%+ confidence went 8-2, precisely the type of conversion rate we'd expect given the aggregate probability. The Reds-Cubs and Marlins-Nationals misses both came in close-spread matchups where underlying metrics suggested competitive games—exactly the type of variance we account for in our expected value calculations.

## Key Performance Drivers: What the Data Tells Us

The strongest performances came from our 63% confidence tier—Dodgers, Blue Jays, and Brewers all delivered as expected. These picks were built on robust underlying metrics: favorable park factors, pitcher WAR differentials, and bullpen strength indicators all aligned. The Brewers' dominance over Texas exemplifies how multiple sabermetric factors can compound into high-probability outcomes.

Our lowest-confidence pick, the Royals at 52%, still converted—a reminder that narrow edges still carry value over large sample sizes. The -110 pricing on this game suggested the market agreed with our assessment of its competitive nature.

## Loss Analysis: Understanding Variance

The Cubs and Nationals victories over our selected teams merit examination. In the Cubs-Reds game, Cincinnati's 61% probability was built on starting pitching advantage, but late-inning leverage situations can overwhelm early-game metrics. The Nationals-Marlins result similarly came down to high-leverage moments where small sample variance dominates.

These outcomes don't invalidate the model—they confirm it. A 61% win probability explicitly acknowledges a 39% chance of the opposite outcome. Over season-long samples, these probabilities converge to their expected values.

## Looking Ahead: No Games Tomorrow

With no games scheduled for August 29th, we have an opportunity to refine our models with fresh data from today's outcomes. The off-day allows for deeper regression analysis and recalibration of pitcher rest effects and bullpen usage patterns that will inform upcoming series.

Today's 11-4 performance reinforces our quantitative approach. The model doesn't promise perfection—it promises probabilistic accuracy over time, and that's exactly what we're seeing in the aggregate results.
